Thank you very much for taking the time to carry out these searches and for your detailed response.

I am also grateful for the information about the Post Office family history records. My main interest is not that Mr Williams was necessarily a Post Office employee, but whether the individual mentioned in contemporary accounts as assisting Marconi at Great House Farm can be identified. Family history passed down through my great grandfather's line suggests that a Mr Williams of Great House Farm assisted Marconi during his South Wales experiments, and I am trying to establish whether this can be connected to my ancestor.

If possible, could you let me know whether the search you carried out included any of the following terms or collections, as this may help me understand the scope of the search:

  *   Great House Farm (Llandough/Penarth)
  *   Llandough
  *   Lavernock
  *   Marconi
  *   wireless telegraphy demonstrations (1897)
  *   GPO Telegraph Department / Engineering Department

I will also contact Glamorgan Archives, as you suggest, since local newspapers, estate records, or correspondence may contain information not held in the national collections.

Thank you again for your assistance. Your guidance has helped narrow down where the relevant evidence is most likely to survive.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear Archive Team,

I am conducting historical research into the General Post Office's involvement in Guglielmo Marconi's wireless demonstrations in South Wales during 1897.

Post Office Ltd has advised that your archive is the most likely repository for surviving historic GPO records relating to this period.

I would be grateful if you could search for any records relating to:

  *   Great House Farm, Llandough, near Penarth, Cardiff (not Great House Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge).
  *   Llandough, Penarth, Lavernock and the surrounding wireless demonstration sites.
  *   Guglielmo Marconi's 1897 demonstrations.
  *   GPO Telegraph or Engineering Department records concerning these demonstrations.
  *   Correspondence, reports, notebooks, diaries, staff lists, expense █████, photographs or plans relating to engineers or officials present.
  *   Any references to Mr Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough, who family history suggests assisted Marconi before, during or after his stay at the property.

If records relating specifically to Mr Williams cannot be located, I would also appreciate details of any records identifying GPO personnel, visitors or local residents connected with the demonstrations, as these may help establish the historical context.

If another archive holds any of these records, I would be grateful if you could advise where I should direct my enquiry.

Mr Williams of Great House Farm was my great grandad. I am trying to ascertain if the Mr Williams post office worker, mentioned helping Marconi in the article, was the same man as my great grandfather. I am also looking for any more connections between my family, my former home and Marconi and the radio experiments at lavernock point. Which I understand were already underway before Marconi arrived to South Wales.

Thank you for your time and assistance. I look forward to your response.

Kind regards,



Requester

Dear Mathilde,

Thank you for your further reply and for carrying out the searches.

I appreciate your assistance, but I would like to clarify the scope and
conclusions of the search, as several points remain unresolved.

Firstly, I should correct one detail: the individual I am researching is *Mr
Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough near Penarth*, not "Mr William".
The surname is significant because family history suggests that my
great-grandfather, Mr Williams of Great House Farm, assisted Guglielmo
Marconi during the 1897 South Wales wireless experiments.

I fully understand that the absence of a result within the Postal Museum
catalogue does not necessarily mean that no such person or record existed.
However, I would be grateful if you could clarify the following:

   1. *Search methodology*

Could you confirm exactly which catalogue collections, series, or record
groups were searched for:

   - Great House Farm, Llandough (Penarth)
   - Llandough
   - Lavernock
   - Marconi
   - wireless telegraphy demonstrations (1897)
   - GPO Telegraph Department
   - Engineering Department
   - Williams / Mr Williams


   2. *Scope of the negative result*

When you state that "nothing relevant came up", does this mean:

   - no indexed catalogue entries were found in Postal Museum collections;
   - no digitised records were found;
   - or that physical archival holdings were also checked?


   3. *Records relating to GPO personnel*

You mentioned that most Marconi and Telegraph Department records are held
at BT Archives. Could you confirm whether the Postal Museum holds any
catalogue references, finding aids, or transferred-record information
indicating where the relevant GPO engineering correspondence, reports,
notebooks, or staff records may have been moved?

   4. *The Williams connection*

The question I am trying to establish is not necessarily whether Mr
Williams was a Post Office employee. He may instead have been the
owner/occupier of Great House Farm who assisted Marconi locally.

Could you therefore confirm whether your search included references to:

   - private individuals assisting demonstrations;
   - hosts or local contacts connected with Marconi's experiments;
   - correspondence mentioning residents of Llandough, Penarth, or
   Lavernock?

I appreciate that the absence of a catalogue entry cannot prove that an
event or person did not exist, particularly where local residents or
private landowners were involved.

My aim is simply to establish the evidential trail: whether the Mr Williams
mentioned in contemporary accounts can be identified, and whether surviving
records connect him with Great House Farm and Marconi's experiments.

Thank you again for your assistance. I would be grateful for any further
clarification on the above points before I proceed to BT Archives and
Glamorgan Archives.

Kind regards,

Requester

records.transcript:
Dear Patricia Reynolds,

Thank you for your response of 30 July 2026 (Case number CAS-343481-X5H3M6).

I note your advice that The National Archives is not the primary repository
for the material described in my original enquiry. However, my enquiry also
concerns whether The National Archives holds any recorded information
relating to the existence, transfer, retention, destruction, or absence of
such records.

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000, I request confirmation of any
recorded information held by The National Archives relating to Great House
Farm / Ty Mawr, Llandough (Glamorgan), including historical references
under alternative descriptions such as Cedfin or equivalent contemporary
descriptions.

Specifically, please confirm whether The National Archives holds:

   1. *Manorial and estate records*

Any catalogue entries, Manorial Documents Register information, finding
aids, transfer records, or related documentation concerning:

   - the Manor of Llandough (Glamorgan);
   - pre-1667 references to occupants, customary tenants, holdings,
   surveys, rentals, terriers, or court rolls;
   - Vaughan family estate holdings at Llandough;
   - Great House Farm / Ty Mawr or any earlier description of the holding.

Please include any references to HMC9/311 or related archival series.

   2. *Records concerning disposal, destruction, or transfer of records*

Any recorded information showing:

   - whether records relating to Great House Farm, Llandough, the Bute
   Estate, Vaughan family papers, or associated land records were ever
   transferred to The National Archives;
   - whether any such records were destroyed, and if so:
      - what records were destroyed;
      - when they were destroyed;
      - under which retention schedule, disposal authority, or policy;
      - which body authorised or carried out the destruction.

If no such records are held, please confirm whether any disposal or
transfer records indicate that relevant material was never deposited or was
destroyed elsewhere.

   3. *Legal and court records*

Any central court records, indexes, correspondence, or administrative
records concerning:

   - possession or title disputes involving Great House Farm / Ty Mawr;
   - Western Ground Rents Ltd;
   - BP Pension Trust Ltd;
   - BP Properties Ltd;
   - Mountjoy Ltd;
   - the proceedings connected with *BP Properties Ltd v Buckler* [1987]
   EWCA Civ 2.


   4. *Estate transfers and ownership records*

Any government-held correspondence, files, or records relating to:

   - the Bute Estate;
   - the 1938 sale or transfer of Great House Farm;
   - Western Ground Rents Ltd acquisition;
   - BP Pension Trust/BP Properties involvement;
   - any government department involvement in the property.


   5. *Family correspondence and related records*

Any correspondence, reports, enquiries, or administrative records held by
The National Archives involving:

   - Mary Williams;
   - Fred Buckler;
   - William Buckler;
   - the Williams/Buckler family;
   - Great House Farm / Ty Mawr;
   - Bute Estate representatives;
   - Western Ground Rents;
   - BP entities.


   6. *1980–1988 period and demolition/eviction matters*

Any records concerning:

   - the public campaign regarding Great House Farm;
   - parliamentary correspondence or government enquiries;
   - the 1988 eviction/demolition;
   - Cadw or government communications;
   - European Commission of Human Rights Application 14464/88 (Buckler v
   United Kingdom).

If any relevant information is held, please provide catalogue references,
descriptions, and access arrangements.

If no relevant information is held, please confirm:

   - the searches undertaken;
   - the catalogues, databases, and record series searched;
   - whether any relevant records were ever held and subsequently
   transferred, destroyed, or disposed of.

I am pursuing parallel enquiries with the National Library of Wales,
Glamorgan Archives and other repositories. This request is specifically
directed at recorded information held by The National Archives.

Yours sincerely,

Requester

Dear Requester,

I searched our archive's catalogued, for all catalogued and uncatalogued items, using the following keywords:

  *   Great House Farm
  *   Llandough
  *   Lavernock
Result: no item is held in our archives using these words in the description.
Concerning the below keywords:

  *   Penarth
  *   wireless demonstrations
  *   GPO Telegraph Department
  *   Engineering Department
  *   Williams / Mr Williams
Result: Some items held in our archives came up with those keywords, but when reading the description field on our catalogue, they turned out to be unrelated to the 1897 wireless telegraphy demonstration. Most were dated to before or after 1897. Many came up on our online catalogue, but they are held at BT Archives, therefore, we won't have any more information. This is what I meant by 'nothing relevant came up' - despite corresponding keyword, the dates or the content aren't related to your enquiry.
The physical archives were not checked as all information on our files are recorded on our archival cataloguing system, which is what I used to search information and keyword. Because the few records that seemed relevant are held at BT Archives, only they can inform you of the digitised or non-digitised status of the items.
Although the items held at BT Archives come up in our archival cataloguing system, you would need to contact directly for more information.
For your questions in 4. On the link with Mr Williams, nothing came up about people who participated to the demonstrations.
You can search our online catalogue here: https://catalogue.postalmuseum.org/
And here is the link to the catalogue of BT Archives: https://www.digitalarchives.bt.com/Calmview/
I hope this helps,
Best regards,

Dear Mathilde,

Thank you for your further reply and for carrying out the searches.

I appreciate your assistance, but I would like to clarify the scope and conclusions of the search, as several points remain unresolved.

Firstly, I should correct one detail: the individual I am researching is Mr Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough near Penarth, not "Mr William". The surname is significant because family history suggests that my great-grandfather, Mr Williams of Great House Farm, assisted Guglielmo Marconi during the 1897 South Wales wireless experiments.

I fully understand that the absence of a result within the Postal Museum catalogue does not necessarily mean that no such person or record existed. However, I would be grateful if you could clarify the following:

  1.  Search methodology

Could you confirm exactly which catalogue collections, series, or record groups were searched for:

  *   Great House Farm, Llandough (Penarth)
  *   Llandough
  *   Lavernock
  *   Marconi
  *   wireless telegraphy demonstrations (1897)
  *   GPO Telegraph Department
  *   Engineering Department
  *   Williams / Mr Williams

  1.  Scope of the negative result

When you state that "nothing relevant came up", does this mean:

  *   no indexed catalogue entries were found in Postal Museum collections;
  *   no digitised records were found;
  *   or that physical archival holdings were also checked?

  1.  Records relating to GPO personnel

You mentioned that most Marconi and Telegraph Department records are held at BT Archives. Could you confirm whether the Postal Museum holds any catalogue references, finding aids, or transferred-record information indicating where the relevant GPO engineering correspondence, reports, notebooks, or staff records may have been moved?

  1.  The Williams connection

The question I am trying to establish is not necessarily whether Mr Williams was a Post Office employee. He may instead have been the owner/occupier of Great House Farm who assisted Marconi locally.

Could you therefore confirm whether your search included references to:

  *   private individuals assisting demonstrations;
  *   hosts or local contacts connected with Marconi's experiments;
  *   correspondence mentioning residents of Llandough, Penarth, or Lavernock?

I appreciate that the absence of a catalogue entry cannot prove that an event or person did not exist, particularly where local residents or private landowners were involved.

My aim is simply to establish the evidential trail: whether the Mr Williams mentioned in contemporary accounts can be identified, and whether surviving records connect him with Great House Farm and Marconi's experiments.

Thank you again for your assistance. I would be grateful for any further clarification on the above points before I proceed to BT Archives and Glamorgan Archives.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear Archive Team,

I am conducting historical research into the General Post Office's involvement in Guglielmo Marconi's wireless demonstrations in South Wales during 1897.

Post Office Ltd has advised that your archive is the most likely repository for surviving historic GPO records relating to this period.

I would be grateful if you could search for any records relating to:

  *   Great House Farm, Llandough, near Penarth, Cardiff (not Great House Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge).
  *   Llandough, Penarth, Lavernock and the surrounding wireless demonstration sites.
  *   Guglielmo Marconi's 1897 demonstrations.
  *   GPO Telegraph or Engineering Department records concerning these demonstrations.
  *   Correspondence, reports, notebooks, diaries, staff lists, expense █████, photographs or plans relating to engineers or officials present.
  *   Any references to Mr Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough, who family history suggests assisted Marconi before, during or after his stay at the property.

If records relating specifically to Mr Williams cannot be located, I would also appreciate details of any records identifying GPO personnel, visitors or local residents connected with the demonstrations, as these may help establish the historical context.

If another archive holds any of these records, I would be grateful if you could advise where I should direct my enquiry.

Mr Williams of Great House Farm was my great grandad. I am trying to ascertain if the Mr Williams post office worker, mentioned helping Marconi in the article, was the same man as my great grandfather. I am also looking for any more connections between my family, my former home and Marconi and the radio experiments at lavernock point. Which I understand were already underway before Marconi arrived to South Wales.

Thank you for your time and assistance. I look forward to your response.

Kind regards,



Requester

Mathilde,

Thank you for clarifying the search methodology. Your explanation is
helpful, particularly the distinction between records appearing in the
Postal Museum catalogue and records physically held at BT Archives.

Before I proceed to BT Archives, I would like to make sure I understand the
limits of the search correctly and avoid unnecessarily duplicating it.

There are a few further points which I would be grateful if you could
clarify.

*1. Date range*

Was the search for the various names and locations conducted across the
surrounding period, or was material effectively assessed only against the
1897 demonstration?

Could you confirm whether *1895–1900*, including 1896, 1898, 1899 and 1900,
was searched?

This is important because I am investigating not only the demonstration
itself but also possible preparations beforehand and correspondence or
reports afterwards.

*2. Catalogue results which were considered unrelated*

You mentioned that some results appeared for terms including Penarth,
wireless demonstrations, GPO Telegraph Department, Engineering Department
and Williams, but that they were considered unrelated after examination of
their catalogue descriptions.

Would it be possible to provide the *catalogue reference numbers and
descriptions of those records*, even where you consider them unrelated,
together with the reason they were excluded?

I would prefer to examine those references myself rather than inadvertently
overlooking something that may become relevant when considered alongside
other records.

*3. Scope of the catalogue*

You have explained that the physical archives were not separately checked
because the information is recorded on the archival cataloguing system.

Could you confirm whether this means that *all existing Postal Museum
archival holdings, including uncatalogued or incompletely catalogued
material, are represented in the system searched*, or whether there are
categories of physical material which may not yet be represented?

*4. Restricted, closed or unprocessed material*

Were any records identified which could potentially relate to the subject
but which were unavailable because they were restricted, closed,
uncatalogued, unprocessed or otherwise inaccessible?

If so, I would be grateful for the relevant reference numbers and any
applicable access restrictions.

*5. Records transferred to BT Archives*

You explained that relevant telecommunications material appearing in the
catalogue is held at BT Archives.

Could you confirm whether the Postal Museum retains any *transfer records,
accession records, finding aids or other information identifying the
particular GPO/Telegraph/Engineering records which were transferred to BT
Archives*?

If there are catalogue references which would help BT Archives locate the
underlying material, I would be very grateful for those.

*6. The Williams connection*

The purpose of the search for Williams is not to establish that Mr Williams
was a Post Office employee.

The family tradition concerns *a local Mr Williams of Great House Farm,
Llandough near Penarth*, who may have assisted Marconi locally.
Consequently, a relevant record might describe him as a local resident,
landowner, farmer, host, assistant, carrier, messenger, proprietor or other
private individual rather than as Post Office personnel.

Could you therefore confirm whether the search for Williams included
references of this kind, rather than only Post Office employees or
personnel records?

Similarly, were variants such as *Mr Williams, W. Williams, William
Williams and Williams* considered?

*7. Preparatory and follow-up records*

Could the search also be considered in terms of records concerning:

   - preparations for the South Wales experiments;
   - arrangements made with local residents or property owners;
   - visits to or use of private premises;
   - transport or movement of equipment;
   - correspondence immediately before or after the experiments;
   - follow-up reports;
   - subsequent demonstrations or experiments in the area;
   - photographs, plans, maps or other material which might identify
   locations or participants.

I appreciate that you may ultimately conclude that none of these are held
by the Postal Museum. I am simply trying to establish precisely what
evidence has and has not survived, and where the relevant archival trail
now leads.

Finally, if the Postal Museum has any *contemporary publications,
newspaper-cutting collections, photographs, finding aids or other material
concerning the South Wales Marconi experiments*, even where they do not
specifically mention Great House Farm or Mr Williams, I would be grateful
for those references as well.

Thank you again for your assistance. Your clarification has helped
considerably in narrowing the search, and I appreciate your taking the time
to establish exactly what the Postal Museum catalogue can and cannot tell
me.

Kind regards,

Requester

records.transcript:
Dear Dr. Driver,

I hope this message finds you well. I wanted first to offer my sincere
congratulations to you and the RCAHMW team on your recent aerial
discoveries. There is something almost magical about the way a sustained
spell of dry, sunny weather can strip back the concealment of centuries —
revealing sites of profound historical importance that grass and topsoil
have kept hidden from view for generations. It is a powerful reminder of
how much of our past lies just beneath the surface, waiting for the right
conditions to bring it back into the light.

I write to you, however, about a site whose concealment has not been
botanical, but bureaucratic and procedural. My family’s history — that of
Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan — has been covered
up not by grass, but by what I can only describe, with careful precision,
as a major scandal of documentary disappearance, procedural irregularity,
and the systematic obscuring of a separate legal title.

The farm, which stood beside St Dochdwy’s Church from at least the 13th
century (and possibly as early as 1215), was home to the Williams family
from 1667 and later the Buckler line. In 1876, the Bute Estate severed 33
acres for the Llandough Limeworks. Family █████, supported by estate
records, indicates that following this severance, the farmhouse, garden and
curtilage may have been treated as a separate legal parcel — a freehold
distinct from the surrounding agricultural leasehold. Yet this distinction,
if it existed, was progressively obscured through decades of litigation,
missing title deeds, and what appears to have been a conflation of two
distinct legal interests.

By the time of the 1987 Court of Appeal decision in BP Properties Ltd v
Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2, the question of historical title had never been
judicially determined. The court ruled on possession and the effect of a
1974 unilateral licence on adverse possession; it did not rule on whether
the Williams family held a separate freehold to the farmhouse plot. The
original Land Registry first-registration bundle (WA231076 / WA240304)
remains inaccessible following an FOI refusal. The 1971 Ordnance Survey
records have not been examined for descriptor shifts. And the 1667
transaction deed — a 999-year lease, effectively a virtual freehold — has
never been located.

The farm was demolished in December 1988. A 1994 rescue excavation by
Cotswold Archaeological Trust revealed 1,026 early-medieval inhumation
burials — the largest such population yet recovered from Wales — yet the
demolition proceeded without archaeological condition. The RCAHMW’s own
1974 floor plan (ST 16817331, H.W. Thomas) documented late 17th–19th
century features shortly before the final litigation. LiDAR data now show
anomalous features near the former site that may indicate a far larger
Roman landscape than previously understood.

What I am asking, Dr. Driver, is whether the RCAHMW — with its unique
statutory role in recording and protecting the historic environment of
Wales — might look again at this site, not with a drone or an aerial
camera, but with the same forensic attention to buried evidence that your
team applies to cropmarks. The grass that covers your aerial sites is
honest; it can be burned away by a hot summer. The concealment surrounding
Great House Farm is of a different order entirely — it lies in missing
documents, inaccessible registries, and a litigation record that addressed
possession while never determining title.

I would welcome the opportunity to share the full reconstructed chronology
(Version 7.0) with you, and to discuss whether RCAHMW records, surveys, or
cartographic archives might hold the key to uncovering what was truly lost
at Llandough.

With warm regards and renewed congratulations on your aerial survey
successes,

Requester

On behalf of the Restored House of Williams / Buckler Family Estate

Great House, Manor of Llandough, Cardiff

📞 █████

Dear Sir/Madam,

This is a separate Freedom of Information request under the Freedom of
Information Act 2000.

It is distinct from my earlier request under your reference 260607013
(submitted 7 June 2026), which concerned the location and access options
for historical court records relating to Great House Farm, Mary
Williams/Buckler, Western Ground Rents and BP (focusing on the 1915, 1955
and 1962 possession proceedings and title/equitable interest evidence).

This new request is limited solely to records of the hearing (or hearings)
at Barry Magistrates Court in late January 1989 at which the Crown
Prosecution Service withdrew the charge arising from the allegation of 29
April 1988 as being “out of time.”

I write under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 to request recorded
information relating to criminal proceedings involving *William Beverly
("Billy") Buckler* arising from events connected with the eviction and
demolition of *Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan*,
during 1988–1989.

I am seeking administrative and recorded information concerning the
handling of these proceedings, rather than personal data contained within
individual case files.

Specifically, I request copies of, or access to, any recorded information
held concerning:

   1.

   The prosecution in which a charge dating from *29 April 1988* alleging
   threatening words or behaviour was withdrawn because the proceedings were
   considered *"out of time."*
   2.

   Any records identifying:
   - the court in which that decision was made;
      - the date of the hearing;
      - the prosecutor involved (reported contemporaneously as *Mr Jeff
      Clarke*);
      - the legal basis upon which the summons was determined to be out of
      time.
   3.

   Records relating to Billy Buckler's appearances before the courts
during *January–March
   1989*, including any surviving:
   - cause lists;
      - court registers;
      - hearing lists;
      - minute books;
      - court log books;
      - bench records;
      - administrative case records;
      - listing records;
      - prosecution correspondence;
      - disposal records; or similar recorded information.
   4.

   Records concerning the proceedings heard in *Cardiff on or about 23
   March 1989*, including recorded information showing:
   - the charges before the court;
      - which charges were proceeded with;
      - which charges were withdrawn or discontinued;
      - the sentence imposed;
      - any recorded fine;
      - any credit given for time already spent in custody.
   5.

   Records concerning charges arising from the *November 1988 eviction of
   Great House Farm*, including allegations of assault and wanton and
   furious driving.
   6.

   Any recorded information concerning:
   - remand or custody records;
      - warrants;
      - bail conditions;
      - injunction-related court administration;
      - any order restricting Billy Buckler from approaching Great House
      Farm.
   7.

   Any retention, destruction or disposal records relating to the above
   court files, including:
   - destruction schedules;
      - retention schedules;
      - disposal certificates;
      - archive transfer records;
      - accession records;
      - file movement records;
      - records identifying when and under what authority any files were
      destroyed or transferred.
   8.

   Any file references, case numbers, register entries or archive
   references relating to these proceedings, even where the substantive files
   no longer survive.

If any of the requested information has been transferred to another body,
such as the relevant archive service or another part of HM Courts &
Tribunals Service or the Ministry of Justice, please identify the receiving
body and any known reference numbers.

If any information is withheld, please specify the exemption relied upon,
explain why it applies, and disclose all reasonably segregable information.

If some parts of this request are more readily available than others, I
would be grateful if those could be disclosed without waiting for the
remainder.

Regards,


Requester

Diolch Rhian,

I'm currently at the Welsh Settlement in South Argentina, otherwise I'd be
there myself. So for our private study and research of our family land,
former home and history, we require photos be permitted to be taken, of
artifacts of interest, so they may be sent to me here.

I'm attempting to reconstruct a replica of our old 800 year old farm house
here as a museum/ open house. We're also trying to understand the
unresolved and ongoing ownership dispute between our family and BP, who
were awarded possession of our farm and home since 1667, which resulted in
us being dispossessed of our ancestral birthland as children in 1988. It's
all a very bizzar case.

The MP for Cardiff covering Llandough responded yesterday and is now aware
of the queries and concerns I'm raising with the case and we appreciate
your cooperation and service and thank you in advance. Subject to me
viewing the records, it's possible I may be warranted in proceeding with a
Senedd public enquiry request, as this could be a matter of public
interest.

No single centralised chronology with all supporting evidence appears to
exist for our land, family and former home and it's history and herritage.
And so this is the purposeful and meaningful work I have chosen to
undertake.

Fascinately world champion boxer Peerless Jim fought his first fight in our
barns. Marconi stayed with us while inventing radio. The house was a court
house and stood on a Roman villa and monestry. It's a trove of hidden
history.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear Requester,

For your question on the date range, I looked at all the files we hold, including before and after the 1897 date. Our records go back to the 17th century and are up to the 21st century. So the dates you mentioned were checked.

2. Catalogue results which were considered unrelated. Would it be possible to provide the catalogue reference numbers and descriptions of those records, even where you consider them unrelated, together with the reason they were excluded?

It would be a very large list of reference numbers to send you, but you can search those key words on the online catalogue here: https://catalogue.postalmuseum.org/

3. Scope of the catalogue. Could you confirm whether this means that all existing Postal Museum archival holdings, including uncatalogued or incompletely catalogued material, are represented in the system searched, or whether there are categories of physical material which may not yet be represented?

For what you will find on the online catalogue: you will only find catalogued items. It includes the ones held at BT Archives. You can tell the difference on where the items are held by looking at the 'Held at' line. Here is an example (unrelated to your area of interest):

[cid:█████]

On my system of archival catalogue: we can search catalogued and uncatalogued items. I also searched the uncatalogued items for your keywords, but only unrelated records came up. In addition to that, most uncatalogued items are records which are less than 20 years old. Any file from c.late 1890s or 1900s is already catalogued so you can't miss them.

4. Restricted, closed or unprocessed material. Were any records identified which could potentially relate to the subject but which were unavailable because they were restricted, closed, uncatalogued, unprocessed or otherwise inaccessible?

The only material that would have restricted access would be records that hold individuals' private information. But considering all the people concerned were alive during the late 1800s and early 1900s, it's very unlikely anyone would still be alive and have any personal information that would still be up-to-date. The other type of records that are restricted are some philatelic items, which don't concern your research.

5. Records transferred to BT Archives. You explained that relevant telecommunications material appearing in the catalogue is held at BT Archives. Could you confirm whether the Postal Museum retains any transfer records, accession records, finding aids or other information identifying the particular GPO/Telegraph/Engineering records which were transferred to BT Archives? If there are catalogue references which would help BT Archives locate the underlying material, I would be very grateful for those.

We don't have any transfer records any longer, it's been too long ago since the records were transferred to BT Archives. But you can easily find out which items are held at BT Archives when searching our online catalogue. See above the screenshot. Using the Finding Number mentioned on one of our online catalogue entries, you should be able to trace the item by contacting BT Archives directly. They are the only ones who have the most up-to-date information about the archival items that were transferred to them.

6. The Williams connection

I'm afraid that we don't hold any record that aren't about postal employees. So we wouldn't be able to find anything about this individual in our records. If there is any record of him in the records held at BT Archives, it's not mentioned in any of the file's descriptions.

7. Preparatory and follow-up records

Concerning all the terms you listed, the relevant records would be kept at BT Archives, so I can't know more about it.

We have some books about Marconi in our reference library, but they are books destined to a general audience and you could find those books in most libraries. It's likely you are already familiar with the titles! Here is the list of books we hold, Online catalogue search 'Marconi lib*'<https://catalogue.postalmuseum.org/collections/search?s=marconi+lib*&qa%5Bkeyword_reference_type%5D=0&qa%5Bpartner%5D=&qa%5Bidentifier%5D=&qa%5Bdate_from%5D=&qa%5Bdate_to%5D=&qa%5Btitle%5D=&qa%5Bperson%5D=&qa%5Bplace%5D=&qa%5Bsubject%5D=&qa%5Bformat%5D=&cbpt=0&cbav=2&cbadvsearchquery=>

I hope those answers will help you in your future research.

Best regards,

Mathilde

Was the search for the various names and locations conducted across the surrounding period, or was material effectively assessed only against the 1897 demonstration?

Could you confirm whether 1895-1900, including 1896, 1898, 1899 and 1900, was searched?

This is important because I am investigating not only the demonstration itself but also possible preparations beforehand and correspondence or reports afterwards.

2. Catalogue results which were considered unrelated

You mentioned that some results appeared for terms including Penarth, wireless demonstrations, GPO Telegraph Department, Engineering Department and Williams, but that they were considered unrelated after examination of their catalogue descriptions.

Would it be possible to provide the catalogue reference numbers and descriptions of those records, even where you consider them unrelated, together with the reason they were excluded?

I would prefer to examine those references myself rather than inadvertently overlooking something that may become relevant when considered alongside other records.

3. Scope of the catalogue

You have explained that the physical archives were not separately checked because the information is recorded on the archival cataloguing system.

Could you confirm whether this means that all existing Postal Museum archival holdings, including uncatalogued or incompletely catalogued material, are represented in the system searched, or whether there are categories of physical material which may not yet be represented?

4. Restricted, closed or unprocessed material

Were any records identified which could potentially relate to the subject but which were unavailable because they were restricted, closed, uncatalogued, unprocessed or otherwise inaccessible?

If so, I would be grateful for the relevant reference numbers and any applicable access restrictions.

5. Records transferred to BT Archives

You explained that relevant telecommunications material appearing in the catalogue is held at BT Archives.

Could you confirm whether the Postal Museum retains any transfer records, accession records, finding aids or other information identifying the particular GPO/Telegraph/Engineering records which were transferred to BT Archives?

If there are catalogue references which would help BT Archives locate the underlying material, I would be very grateful for those.

6. The Williams connection

The purpose of the search for Williams is not to establish that Mr Williams was a Post Office employee.

The family tradition concerns a local Mr Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough near Penarth, who may have assisted Marconi locally. Consequently, a relevant record might describe him as a local resident, landowner, farmer, host, assistant, carrier, messenger, proprietor or other private individual rather than as Post Office personnel.

Could you therefore confirm whether the search for Williams included references of this kind, rather than only Post Office employees or personnel records?

Similarly, were variants such as Mr Williams, W. Williams, William Williams and Williams considered?

7. Preparatory and follow-up records

Could the search also be considered in terms of records concerning:

  *   preparations for the South Wales experiments;
  *   arrangements made with local residents or property owners;
  *   visits to or use of private premises;
  *   transport or movement of equipment;
  *   correspondence immediately before or after the experiments;
  *   follow-up reports;
  *   subsequent demonstrations or experiments in the area;
  *   photographs, plans, maps or other material which might identify locations or participants.

I appreciate that you may ultimately conclude that none of these are held by the Postal Museum. I am simply trying to establish precisely what evidence has and has not survived, and where the relevant archival trail now leads.

Finally, if the Postal Museum has any contemporary publications, newspaper-cutting collections, photographs, finding aids or other material concerning the South Wales Marconi experiments, even where they do not specifically mention Great House Farm or Mr Williams, I would be grateful for those references as well.

Thank you again for your assistance. Your clarification has helped considerably in narrowing the search, and I appreciate your taking the time to establish exactly what the Postal Museum catalogue can and cannot tell me.

Kind regards,

Requester

I am researching the General Post Office involvement in Guglielmo Marconi's South Wales wireless telegraphy experiments during 1897, particularly the experiments between Lavernock Point and Flat Holm.

The Postal Museum has advised that the relevant GPO Telegraph Department and Engineering Department records are likely to be held by BT Archives. They confirmed that their own searches of Postal Museum holdings found no relevant records and that surviving telecommunications material from this period is likely to be within the collections transferred to BT Archives.

I would be grateful if you could advise on the relevant surviving records and catalogue references.

My research concerns:

  *   Marconi's 1897 South Wales wireless experiments;
  *   Lavernock Point and Flat Holm;
  *   Penarth and Llandough (near Penarth);
  *   the involvement of the GPO Telegraph Department and Engineering Department;
  *   any surviving correspondence, reports, notebooks, engineering records, plans, photographs or administrative records connected with the experiments.

I am particularly interested in identifying any references to local residents or private individuals who assisted Marconi or GPO engineers. Family history suggests that a Mr Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough, may have assisted with the experiments locally. I appreciate that such a person may not appear in catalogue descriptions if he was a private individual rather than a GPO employee.

  *   Marconi
  *   Guglielmo Marconi

  *   Lavernock
  *   Penarth
  *   Llandough
  *   Great House Farm
  *   Williams
  *   W. Williams
  *   William Williams
  *   Mr Williams

If relevant records exist, I would be grateful for the catalogue references, file descriptions and dates so that I can identify the material for further research.

I would also appreciate any guidance on whether there are related collections, transferred Post Office records, or finding aids that may not be obvious from the online catalogue.

Thank you very much for your assistance.

Kind regards,

Dear Ms James,

Thank you for your considered response.

I understand and accept that the Committee does not have a remit to
adjudicate upon an individual dispute, determine whether a historical
decision was lawful, or direct Cadw to reopen a particular case. My
submission was deliberately framed so as not to ask the Committee to do any
of those things.

I would, however, respectfully clarify one point, because I am concerned
that the nature of the request may have been characterised more narrowly
than intended.

The attached report expressly states that it is *not a legal challenge, a
forensic proof of wrongdoing, a complaint seeking adjudication, or a demand
for reversal of the 1988 decision*. Its stated purpose is historical record
correction, archival explanation and administrative acknowledgement. In
particular, it asks for an explanation of why almost none of the records
concerning the 1988 assessment survive, whether that reflects the
applicable record-retention arrangements, and whether the surviving
independent evidence should be properly reflected in the permanent public
record.

The central issue therefore extends beyond the merits of the individual
1988 listing assessment.

Cadw's 2026 FOI response confirms that an assessment took place, but that
only two exterior photographs now survive; the assessment report, reasons
for refusal, site notes, internal recommendations and consultation
correspondence are no longer available. The report does not assert that
this proves wrongdoing. Rather, it identifies a straightforward
public-administration question: *how can the adequacy and evidential basis
of an irreversible public heritage decision be understood or scrutinised
when the underlying administrative record no longer survives?*

That seems potentially relevant to the Committee's stated function of
scrutinising the administration and accountability of Welsh Government and
associated public bodies, even if the Committee cannot itself determine
whether the 1988 decision was correct.

I am therefore not asking the Committee to investigate the Buckler family's
historical dispute with BP, adjudicate upon the 1988 decision, or direct
Cadw to reverse anything. The specific administrative questions raised in
the report are instead:

   1. What record-retention arrangements applied to the 1988 assessment?
   2. Why do the assessment report, reasons, site notes and consultation
   records no longer survive?
   3. Were the records destroyed under an applicable retention policy or
   other authority, and were they considered for transfer to the appropriate
   archival institution?
   4. Is the present position consistent with Welsh Government/Cadw
   expectations for the preservation of records concerning significant
   heritage decisions?
   5. Are current arrangements sufficient to ensure that comparable
   heritage assessments, particularly where a building is under imminent
   threat of demolition, are properly documented and retained?

These are not questions that require the Committee to determine the rights
of either party to the original dispute. They concern *administrative
practice, institutional record-keeping and the ability of the Senedd and
the public to scrutinise decisions taken by public bodies*. The report
specifically asks Cadw to explain the archival position and review its
current record-keeping practices for this reason.

I would therefore be grateful if the Committee could reconsider whether the
broader administrative and accountability issue falls within its scrutiny
function, even if the Committee cannot examine the underlying individual
dispute.

If the Committee considers that it nevertheless cannot engage with the
matter, I would appreciate clarification as to *which Senedd or Welsh
Government scrutiny, oversight, archival or complaints mechanism is
considered appropriate for raising a documented concern about the absence
of the administrative record of a historical Cadw decision and the
implications this has for public accountability*.

For completeness, I should also emphasise that the report itself
deliberately recognises the limits of the surviving evidence. It does not
claim that Cadw acted unlawfully or in bad faith, and it expressly
acknowledges that the absence of the 1988 working papers means that the
assessment cannot now be reconstructed definitively.

My objective is therefore quite limited: *to ensure that the surviving
evidence is preserved, that the archival gap is properly explained, and
that the public record accurately distinguishes what is established from
what can no longer be verified.*

I hope that clarification assists, and I would be grateful if you could
confirm whether the Committee is able to consider the matter from that
wider public-administration and accountability perspective.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear Mr Haste,

Thank you for your letter of *30 July 2026* concerning reference *N610CGV*
and the surviving records relating to the first registration of titles
*WA231076
and WA240304* at Great House Farm, Llandough.

I am writing to clarify the factual contents of the surviving
first-registration records and to identify the appropriate documents for
inspection/copying. *This is not a request to reopen my previous complaint,
nor am I asking HM Land Registry to determine the historical ownership
dispute.*

I would be grateful if you could clarify the following.
1. The 1971 Abstract of Title

You previously confirmed that a *1971 Abstract of Title* was seen in
connection with this matter.

Please confirm:

   - whether it still survives;
   - which title/file it relates to;
   - its item or document reference within the surviving records; and
   - whether it is available for inspection or copying.

2. The “question or doubt” certificate

Please confirm where in the surviving first-registration material the
certificate/declaration appears in which the applicant's solicitors stated
that they were *“not aware of any question or doubt affecting the title.”*

In particular, please confirm whether this forms part of the *Form 1E dated
30 November 1982*, or is a separate surviving document.
3. What the first-registration file records about other interests

Please confirm whether any of the surviving first-registration documents
contain any reference to:

   - *Mary Williams*;
   - *Fred Buckler*;
   - *William (Billy) Buckler*;
   - *Great House Farm / Ty Mawr* and its farmhouse, garden or curtilage;
   - any person other than the applicant asserting ownership or another
   interest in the land;
   - possession proceedings concerning the farmhouse or land; or
   - any objection, dispute, question or doubt concerning title.

I am asking this *solely as a factual question about the contents of the
surviving records*.

If no such reference appears in the surviving first-registration material,
confirmation of that fact would be sufficient.
4. Identification of the surviving documents

Your 30 July letter identifies, amongst other things, the *Form 1E, A13-DL
list of documents lodged and correspondence from Linklaters & Paines*.

Please identify the specific item numbers I should request by *Form OC2* to
obtain the fullest available surviving first-registration record,
particularly:

   - the title evidence submitted by the applicant;
   - the 1971 Abstract of Title, if it survives;
   - the A13-DL list of documents lodged;
   - correspondence with Linklaters & Paines;
   - examiner's notes, requisitions, memoranda or file notes, if any
   survive; and
   - any document recording the basis upon which the Registrar accepted the
   applicant's title.

If any of these categories do not survive, please identify which ones do
not.
5. Historic records relevant to identifying the land

I also wish to ensure that the correct physical parcel is being compared
with the land registered in 1982–83.

During recent research at the Glamorgan Archives, I have located historic
material concerning Great House Farm/Ty Mawr, including:

   - the *6 November 1877 Bute Estate counterpart lease to John Williams*;
   - the *1872 Llandough Rate Book*;
   - the *1924 and 1938 Great House Farm sale particulars and associated OS
   parcel references*; and
   - historic plans and notes concerning the farmhouse, gardens and
   associated boundaries.

These records appear potentially relevant to identifying the historic
extent and boundaries of the farmhouse and curtilage.

I am *not asking HM Land Registry to determine the legal effect of those
documents*. I simply wish to establish whether the documents submitted
during the 1982/83 first-registration process identify the same physical
parcel and, if so, what documentary evidence was relied upon to establish
that identity.
6. Subsequent planning record

For completeness, the later planning record also contains a significant
contemporaneous document: *BP Properties Ltd's Certificate A dated 16
October 1989 in respect of outline application 89/01396/OUT*, in which BP
certified its position concerning ownership of the application land.

Again, I am not asking HM Land Registry to determine the effect of that
document. I mention it only because it makes it particularly important for
my research to establish precisely *what documentary evidence was actually
before the Registrar in 1982–83*, several years before that planning
certification.
7. Form OC2

I am particularly keen to avoid submitting an unnecessarily broad OC2
request.

If you could therefore identify the *specific item numbers* from your 30
July schedule which would provide the fullest surviving first-registration
record, I can request those documents directly.

In particular, I would appreciate confirmation of the items corresponding
to the *Form 1E, A13-DL list, title evidence, Linklaters & Paines
correspondence, the 1971 Abstract of Title, and any examiner/requisition
material that survives*.

Thank you for your assistance. I would be grateful for a substantive
clarification of the above points so that I can proceed with a properly
targeted inspection/copy request.

Regards,

*Requester*
*Sgt (Ret’d)*
